newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem accepts justice chief's resignation. [CORRECTED 14:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem accepts justice chief's resignation. [CORRECTED 14:30 GMT]

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem on Thursday (corrects day) accepted the resignation of his justice minister who acknowledged contacts with a tycoon suspected in a murder case and alleged to be a mobster, a presidential spokesman said.
Spokesman Raul Delgado told reporters in a terse statement that Menem was replacing the minister, Elias Jassan, with the current ambassador to Washington, Raul Granillo Ocampo.

Jassan, as well as Interior Minister Carlos Corach and Menem's Chief of Staff Alberto Kohan, have been accused by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo of manipulating the courts to protect tycoon Alfredo Yabran's alleged criminal activities. Cavallo has accused Yabran of being the "head of the mafia."

They have all denied the charges and Yabran denies any wrongdoing. But Jassan was caught lying a week ago when he first denied he knew Yabran, then had to admit to receiving more than 100 phone calls from the businessman's office.

Yabran is also suspected by police as their "only lead" in investigations into who ordered the murder of photographer Jose Luis Cabezas in January. Cabezas, who took photos of Yabran for Noticias magazine, was shot and his body burned.
